title: One Combined Annual Entitlement Across a Member's Healthy Options Cards
content:
Where a member holds more than one allowance programme, the loads are added together against one combined annual cap: the programmes are separate cards but a single entitlement. This is the standing basis for the Supplemental Benefit Allowance Programmes.

1. **The cap bites on the load.** A load that would take the member's combined loads for the benefit year past the combined annual allowance cap is made only up to the distance remaining, and the member is told which card was reduced and why.
2. **What counts toward the cap.** What counts toward the cap is what has been loaded less what has expired or been forfeited, so an allowance the member never had the chance to spend never uses up their entitlement. The figure is taken across every allowance programme the member holds in that benefit year.
3. **Which cap applies where the tiers differ.** Where the member holds programmes of different tiers, the cap taken is the highest cap among the programmes held, never the sum of the caps.
4. **Spending is not pooled.** Money on one card cannot be spent at a retailer only the other card is good for, and the member is told which card to use rather than being left to find out at the till.

**A worked illustration on hypothetical figures.** Suppose a member's combined loads for the benefit year stand at 1,320.00 USD once expiries and forfeitures have been taken off, and the combined annual allowance cap on their Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card programmes is 1,400.00 USD. A scheduled load of 260.00 USD then falls due. The distance remaining is 80.00 USD, so 80.00 USD is made available and not 260.00 USD, and the member is told which card was reduced and why. Had 100.00 USD of an earlier load already expired unspent, that 100.00 USD would not count toward the cap, and the distance remaining would be 180.00 USD instead.
